text: The project is a software system and needs no special electronic hardware. The prototype was developed and tested on an ordinary laptop. The cloud server planned for deployment is a small virtual machine.

caption: Table 4.1: Hardware used
rows: Laptop with the Windows 11 operating system
Any computer or phone with a current web browser (Chrome was used for testing)
Hardhat local Ethereum node running on the development laptop
Small Oracle Cloud virtual machine, free tier, running Ubuntu and Docker
Three separate computers or accounts, each holding one encrypted key share

caption: Table 4.2: Software used
rows: Runtime for the backend, scripts and tests
Database for roll, sessions and token hashes
Talking to the blockchain from the backend and tools
AES-GCM and RSA-OAEP in the voter's browser
Splitting and rebuilding the election key
Security headers and the content security policy
Container image and automatic HTTPS for the cloud deployment

text: The system was developed in stages, and each stage was tested before the next began: first the smart contract and its tests; then the key ceremony; then the backend with the mock OTP service and the token logic; then the voter and administrator pages; and last a one-button demonstration page and the deployment tooling. The code was organised as follows.

caption: Table 4.3: Organisation of the project code
rows: Express server, mock OTP service, voter hash, token store, blockchain client, one-button mode
Voter page, administrator page and the browser-side ballot encryption
Key ceremony, administrator commands, tally, submit-tally, verify-tally, deployment and demo launcher
Contract tests, backend and cryptography tests

text: Two practical problems found during development deserve mention because they affected correctness. First, sending two transactions quickly one after the other made the library re-use a transaction number, so the second failed; the fix was to turn off the library's short-term cache of the account's transaction count. Second, on a fresh local chain the clock of the chain lagged behind real time, so the contract answered that voting was not yet open; the start-up script now mines a block and uses the chain's own time.
